To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the apical membrane of Calu-3 airway epithelial cells contains a cAMP-activated Cl channel that is identical to CFTR, and a parallel cAMP-activated anion channel that is probably located in tight junctions.

the anion permeation properties of CFTR expressed in Calu 3 cells are very similar to those of the CFTR expressed in other expression systems, and that CFTR in Calul 3 cells is not permeable to physiologically relevant large anions such as ATP, PO4, and SO4.

the cAMP-stimulation of the apical membrane of polarized Cal-u 3 cells results in anion currents that are carried primarily by CFTR and that have a selectivity sequence of Br≥Cl≥SCN>NO3>I≥F>formic acid>HCO3> acetate>propionate>butyrate=PPi=ATP=PO4=0.
